summary: Deployed inventory-api as a systemd-managed service on node1 (RHEL 9), hardened with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 and OOMPolicy=continue so the kernel OOM-killer never selects it. Verified under a real memory-exhaustion test that a deliberately unprotected memory-hog process (oom_score_adj=0) was the one killed by the kernel while inventory-api kept serving without interruption or restart. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot id and service health, rebooted node1 via systemctl reboot, confirmed the boot id changed, and verified inventory-api came back enabled/active and serving correctly post-reboot.
actions_performed: Created inventory-api system user and /opt/inventory-api/app.py (Python HTTP service exposing /health and /inventory on 0.0.0.0:8080)
Created /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service with Restart=always, OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, OOMPolicy=continue; enabled and started it
Verified service active and endpoints responding; confirmed oom_score_adj=-1000 on the running PID
Disabled swap to make OOM triggering deterministic, launched a memory-hog Python process with default oom_score_adj=0
Observed via dmesg that the kernel OOM-killer selected and killed the hog process (pid 1722, oom_score_adj=0), while inventory-api (pid 1651) was untouched and continued serving with unbroken uptime
Re-enabled swap, cleaned up hog scratch files

Captured pre-restart boot id and health baseline, issued sudo systemctl reboot, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed boot id changed, and verified inventory-api was enabled/active and serving post-reboot

evidence.requirement: inventory-api runs as a managed (systemd) service and serves inventory data
evidence.summary: systemd unit created, enabled, started; curl to /health and /inventory returns correct JSON with oom_score_adj confirmed at -1000

evidence.requirement: service survives system-wide OOM by having the memory hog killed instead
evidence.summary: Memory hog (pid 1722, oom_score_adj=0) launched and grew to ~1.8GB RSS; dmesg shows kernel OOM-killer explicitly killed pid 1722 'python3' while inventory-api (pid 1651, oom_score_adj=-1000) remained running continuously (uptime 30s unbroken) and kept serving /health and /inventory correctly
Captured boot_id 55595e92-e932-451b-ac1d-75d72072b358, systemctl is-active=active, and successful /health response prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: node restarted one at a time with native safe reboot, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Issued 'sudo systemctl reboot' backgrounded so the exec call returned 'reboot issued' before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: proof of changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Polling showed connection timeouts/resets during reboot, then a successful read of boot_id b3439b6d-70ac-4e41-8b0b-33e0b2fcaaad, distinct from the pre-restart boot_id, with uptime showing a fresh boot time

evidence.requirement: post-restart recovery of required service and data verified
evidence.summary: inventory-api shown enabled and active with a new PID (699) since the reboot; /health and /inventory endpoints responded correctly; swap restored to 2GiB available
